subject: Auxiliary provider inventory & telemetry sampling details for SIG/CAIQ
messages:
From: Amy Lin <amy.lin@clearsighthealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
Cc: security-team@clearsighthealth.com
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Inventory and sampling evidence for SIG/CAIQ - Clearsight

Karthik,

As part of our SIG/CAIQ assessment I'm collecting an inventory of all auxiliary providers (subprocessors) that touch telemetry or observability data for inference traffic. Two specific asks from our risk team: 

1) A CSV list of providers with what data class they see (metrics, traces, raw request/response, aggregated logs) and whether any PII or customer identifiers are present.
2) A short description (one-paragraph) of how telemetry sampling is implemented (sampling rate defaults, redaction/aggregation applied before export, retention period).

If you have a redacted sample of the export (or README) we can include that in our evidence bundle. We're trying to close this section by EOW — can you confirm what you can provide and an ETA?

Thanks,
Amy Lin
Senior Security Program Manager
Clearsight Health

From: karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
To: Amy Lin <amy.lin@clearsighthealth.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwoodinference.com, priyom_das@redwoodinference.com
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 10:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Inventory and sampling evidence for SIG/CAIQ - Clearsight

Amy — thanks for the clear list of asks. We'll assemble the CSV and a short README describing sampling and redaction. Quick notes up front:

- We maintain a dedicated auxiliary provider roster for telemetry/observability that excludes customer data plane processors. Most telemetry is aggregated and sampled; raw request/response exports are disabled by default and require elevated approvals.
- Estimated ETA: initial CSV + README by end of day (today). If you need raw schema samples, we'll provide a redacted snippet in the README; full raw exports require a data access request and a short MOU.

Looping in Priyom (platform security) and Monica (compliance operations) to drop the inventory and clarify retention.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

From: priyom_das@redwoodinference.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com, Amy Lin <amy.lin@clearsighthealth.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwoodinference.com
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 11:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Inventory and sampling evidence for SIG/CAIQ - Clearsight

Amy / team — attaching the auxiliary provider inventory CSV and a short telemetry sampling README. Summary here: 

- Attachment: redwood_aux_providers_inventory_v1.csv (provider name, service, data types seen, PII flag, region, contractual status)
- Attachment: telemetry_sampling_readme.pdf (explains default sampling: 1% request-level sampling for full traces, 100% metrics aggregation for infrastructure metrics, redaction steps, and 90-day retention for raw telemetry; aggregated metrics retained as per customer plan)

Key points in the README (TL;DR):
- Default sampling is conservative: we only capture full request traces for 1% of traffic; a separate aggregation pipeline collects counters and latency histograms at 100% with no raw request bodies.
- Any export that could contain identifiers is redacted at the ingestion layer: API keys, user_identifiers, and obvious PII fields are removed before persistence.
- We maintain a small set of observability partners (re: CSV) — all are on standard DPA terms and most are SOC 2 Type II compliant; we included compliance notes per provider in the CSV.

Attachments: redwood_aux_providers_inventory_v1.csv (type: text/csv), telemetry_sampling_readme.pdf (type: application/pdf)

If you want a short statement signed by our security team certifying these controls for your SIG pack, we can produce one.

—Priyom
Priyom Das
Senior Platform Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Amy Lin <amy.lin@clearsighthealth.com>
To: priyom_das@redwoodinference.com, karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
Cc: security-team@clearsighthealth.com
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 11:55:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Inventory and sampling evidence for SIG/CAIQ - Clearsight

Thanks Priyom — that looks helpful. A couple quick follow-ups the risk team flagged after a quick skim: 

1) For providers that perform encryption/KMS or key management, can you list the key custody model (customer-managed KMS vs. provider-managed) in the CSV?
2) For the 1% trace sampling: is the sampling deterministic (e.g., hash-based) or random? We need to understand if sampling could bias on a customer identifier.
3) For long-term evidence: would you be able to provide the SOC 2 section or the attestation statement for the top three telemetry vendors listed?

If you can annotate the CSV with those three items, that should close most of our open items. Appreciate the fast turnaround.

Amy

From: karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
To: Amy Lin <amy.lin@clearsighthealth.com>
Cc: priyom_das@redwoodinference.com, monica_patel@redwoodinference.com
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 13:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Inventory and sampling evidence for SIG/CAIQ - Clearsight

Amy — noted. Short answers here and we'll update the CSV within the hour: 

- KMS/key custody: we use provider-managed KMS for platform telemetry by default; for Dedicated/Private customers we support customer-managed KMS (we'll mark per-provider in the CSV).
- Sampling: trace sampling is deterministic by default (hash-based on request ID) so it is stable and not biased by timestamp; we will include the deterministic algorithm description in the README. You can request a non-deterministic/random sample for special audits.
- SOC 2/attestations: we'll attach attestation statements for the top three telemetry vendors where available (many vendors publish SOC 2 reports or provide them on request). Monica will push the vendor SOC attachments to this thread / our secure drive link.

Expect the annotated CSV + updated README + links to vendor attestations shortly.

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
